newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 20.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Finance & Economic minister Kang Kyong-shik held news conference yesterday and said a tight fiscal policy would be implemented with the government cutting its spending by two trillion won.
- The Korean economy grew 7.1 percent in real terms in 1996, down from the 8.9 percent a year earlier, the Bank of Korea said.

- Hanbo Engineering and Construction defaulted on loans on Thursday, and Korea First Bank, its main creditor will seek a third party to take over the company after Hanbo under goes court receivership.

- North Korea appears ready to announce its decision to attend preliminary meeting for the proposed peace talks as the isolated state, facing an imminent "famine", appears to be gearing up for better ties with its archrival South Korea.

- President Kim Young-sam sent personal letters to Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Prime Minister Li Peng thanking their cooperation for the safe passage of Hwang Jang-yop, North Korea's defector, from Beijing to a stopover point in the Philippines.
